title: SRE SLOs, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Review Standards, Operational Tooling, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's SRE guidance for defining and operating SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning practices, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling expectations, and a canonical runbook template. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform owners, service-level owners, and managers responsible for production LLM inference services.

Scope

- Services covered: inference-api, routing-service, cache-service, kv-store, telemetry-ingest, dedicated-gpu-proxy.
- Audience: SREs, service owners, infra engineers, release engineers, and on-call responders.
- Related docs: see related_pages metadata.

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

Goal: Measure reliability in user-facing terms and provide clear actions when budgets are consumed.

SLO model and naming

- Each public-facing service must publish at least one Availability SLO and one Latency SLO.
- SLO names: <service>-availability, <service>-p99-latency, <service>-p95-latency.

Standard SLO targets (default baseline)

| SLO | Metric | Window | Target | Rationale |
|-----|--------|--------|--------|-----------|
| availability | successful requests / total requests | 30d | 99.95% | User-facing uptime for hosted API tier |
| p99 latency | 99th percentile server latency (ms) | 7d | <= 450ms | Latency sensitive for interactive chat |
| p95 latency | 95th percentile server latency (ms) | 7d | <= 150ms | Typical median tail for autoscaled paths |

Error budget policy

- Error budget = 1 - SLO target. Track burn over rolling 7-day and 30-day windows.
- Escalation thresholds:
  1. Green: burn rate <= 1x expected (no action).
  2. Attention: 1x < burn rate <= 3x — Service owner notified; investigate regressions and recent deploys.
  3. Action: 3x < burn rate <= 10x — Pause non-critical deploys; schedule a reliability sprint if sustained > 24h.
  4. Emergency: burn rate > 10x or projected budget exhaustion in < 24h — Pager escalation; invoke incident review and rollback to known-good.

- Mitigations allowed: traffic shaping, reducing feature flags, diverting to lower-cost model variants; all mitigations must be recorded in the incident log and linked to the SLO dashboard.

SLO ownership and publishing

- Owner: service owner (product or engineering) owns SLO definitions and the error budget policy.
- SRE: provides measurement, dashboards, alerting, and tooling.
- Publication: SLOs must be documented in the service confluence page and in the SLO registry (Grafana/Prometheus metadata labels).

2) Capacity Planning

Principles

- Plan for 99th traffic growth scenario + 30% headroom for bursts for urgent customer requests.
- Separate capacity for Dedicated customers with pinned GPU pools; do not allocate shared on-hosted lanes for reserved capacity.
- Use workload-characterization (p50 sequence length, p95 sequence length, model kv cache hit rates) to estimate tokens/sec per GPU slot.

Process and cadence

1. Quarterly capacity review: forecast 3, 6, and 12 month demand per region.
2. Monthly pulse: check capacity utilization, slot saturation, queue wait times; raise capacity change tickets if util > 70% sustained for 24h.
3. Pre-release capacity check: any major release (new model, quantization change, routing change) requires a capacity sign-off (capacity-on-call + infra-owner).

Key metrics to track

- GPU slot utilization (%), average tokens/sec per slot, queue depth (requests waiting > SLO latency target), autoscaler scale events, model-specific CPI (cost per inference), cold-start frequency.

Capacity runbook (high-level)

1. Identify hot paths: use per-route dashboards to find >70% util or rising queue depth.
2. Short-term: increase burst pools, enable additional inference instances with lower batch size.
3. Medium-term: request reserved capacity for Dedicated or add instances in target region.
4. Long-term: optimize model quantization/profile and routing to reduce per-token cost.

3) Reliability Initiatives

- Blameless postmortems for any incident that consumed >25% of a monthly error budget or caused customer SLA impact.
- Quarterly Reliability Sprint: cross-functional initiative to address top 3 reliability risks per service (e.g., KV cache eviction tuning, autoscaler stability, kernel upgrade regressions).
- Automated regression detection: run nightly inference-eval-harness against canary model bundle and alert on quality or latency regressions >5% relative to baseline.

Program examples

- Cache resilience project: add 3-tier cache fallback and per-prefix TTL tuning; target 40% reduction in p99 latency tail for cold-start workloads.
- Autoscaler hardening: reduce oscillation by increasing cool-down from 30s -> 60s and add hysteresis.

4) Incident Review Standards

Goals: Produce fast, blameless, actionable reviews that reduce repeat incidents.

Mandatory fields for postmortem

- Incident ID, severity level, start/end timestamps (UTC), services impacted, customer impact summary, SLOs affected and % of error budget consumed, timeline of events, root cause analysis (RCA), corrective actions, action owners, timeline for remediation, follow-up verification plan.

Severity definitions (examples)

- Sev 1 (Critical): Multi-region outage, >1% of active requests affected, or critical Dedicated customer SLA breach.
- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation for a subset of customers or routes; short-term mitigation required.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized degradations, noisy logs, or non-urgent reliability regressions.

Postmortem process

1. Create incident page within 48 hours of mitigation.
2. Draft RCA within 5 business days.
3. Final review and sign-off by SRE lead and service owner within 10 business days.
4. Track action items in backlog with owner and target completion date; review at weekly reliability standup until closed.

5) Operational Tooling

Required dashboards and alerts

- Per-service SLO dashboard: availability, latency P50/P95/P99, error budget projection, recent deploys, and mitigation notes.
- Capacity dashboard: GPU utilization by pool, tokens/sec, queue depth, cold-start rate, autoscaler events.
- Heatmap: model-specific latency by sequence length and batch size.
- Alerting rules (examples):
  - availability-drop: availability < SLO target over a 5m window -> page P1.
  - p99-latency-tail: p99 > configured threshold for 2 consecutive 5m windows -> page P2.
  - error-budget-accelerated-burn: burn rate > 3x over 6h -> page P2 and notify service owner.

Tooling expectations

- Alert fatigue policy: every paging alert must have an associated runbook and triage owner. Alert tuning reviews quarterly.
- Incident tooling: use pagerduty for escalation, Jira for action items, and a standardized incident page template (this document's postmortem section).
- Observability: traces must be retained for 7 days and logs for 30 days by default for SRE triage. Longer retention is by exception.

6) Canonical Runbook Template (must be used for each critical alert)

- Title: <alert-name> runbook
- Pager: escalation path (on-call -> primary -> secondary -> engineering manager)
- Quick assessment (1-2 lines): "Likely cause: X. Immediate impact: Y"
- Immediate actions (ordered):
  1. Check per-service SLO dashboard and confirm alert context (Grafana link).
  2. Verify recent deploys: check deploy-log and gitsha. Command: `kubectl get deployments -n service -o json | jq .`
  3. Check autoscaler events and queue depth. Command: `curl -s https://monitoring.internal/api/queue?service=<service>`
  4. If error-budget burn high and recent deploy, rollback via release pipeline: `releases rollback <service> <previous-good>` (notify deploy channel).
  5. If capacity-saturation: increase burst pool: `infra up --pool burst --count 2 --region <region>` (notify infra team).
  6. For persistent model regressions, switch routing to compatible model-variant: update policy in routing-service: `POST /routing/v1/override` with model-id.
  7. Document mitigation steps in incident page and add to postmortem actions.

- Verification and recovery checklist:
  - Confirm SLOs returning to green for two consecutive 5m windows.
  - Re-enable paused deploys only on approval by service owner.
  - Create follow-up ticket if fix is required.

Runbook example (availability-drop for inference-api)

1. Pager triggers to on-call.
2. On-call runs `curl -s https://metrics.internal/slo/inference-api/availability?window=5m` and confirms drop.
3. Check recent deploy: `cat /var/log/deploys/inference-api/recent.log` -> roll back if deploy within 10m of incident start.
4. If deploy not culprit, check GPU pool utilization: `grafana link -> GPU pool util` -> add burst nodes.

7) Roles & Ownership

- Service Owner: defines SLOs and approves mitigations.
- SRE On-call: executes runbooks and pages appropriate owners.
- Infra/Capacity Owner: executes capacity changes and reserved capacity requests.
- Observability Owner: maintains dashboards, alert rules, and SLO measurement correctness.

8) KPIs & Dashboards to Drive Reliability

- Error budget consumption by service (30d & 7d).
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) and mean time to recovery (MTTR) per severity.
- Frequency of rollbacks vs. mitigations.
- Capacity headroom by region and model family.

9) Change Management and Releases

- All changes that affect inference runtime (model weights, kernel changes, quantization profiles, routing logic) require a release checklist and a preflight capacity & SLO impact review.
- Canary policy: 5% traffic for 30m, monitor latency and error budget burn; if no anomalies, increase to 25% for 1h, then 100%.

Appendix A — Example SLO config (Prometheus-style label guidance)

- prometheus_job: inference-api
- slo_name: inference-api-p99-latency
- slo_target: "0.995"
- slo_window: "7d"

Appendix B — Common commands and links

- SLO dashboards: https://grafana.internal/dashboards/slo-inference-api
- Deploy pipeline: https://ci.internal/pipelines/inference-api
- Incident template: https://confluence.internal/incidents/template
- Increase burst pool (infra CLI): `infra up --pool burst --count <n> --region <r>`

Appendix C — Verification and audit

- SLO definitions and revisions must be recorded in the service confluence page and in the SLO registry. Significant SLO changes (delta >0.1% target) require sign-off from SRE lead and product manager.
